about: Research sheet for the Connecticut county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Connecticut
phones_sentence: District office phones come from the Office of Advocacy and Assistance page. Connecticut services are organized by town; each county card names the towns served by another office.

offices.source_title: Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs: Office of Advocacy and Assistance district offices
offices.note: Veteran Service Officers help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and state benefits at no charge.
offices.selection: Connecticut has no county veterans offices. The department’s Where to Get Help page (read in full) assigns each town to one of five district offices, and the State Library’s town list (read in full) gives each town’s county. Each county shows the district serving most of its towns, with the other districts as other offices. The town list does not show Greenwich, Shelton or Windsor; those cards say to call the main line. Goshen appears twice on the page (Districts 4 and 5); it is shown with District 5, like its neighbors.

aging.source_title: Connecticut Department of Aging and Disability Services: 2024 CHOICES training flyer (Area Agency on Aging towns served)
aging.source_scope: The towns each Area Agency on Aging serves; read in full. Agency addresses and phones come from the Department of Aging and Disability Services Additional Resources page (https://portal.ct.gov/ads/additional-resources; read in full). The flyer omits Meriden; the 2022 CHOICES brochure lists it with South Central (search excerpt). Each county shows the agency serving most of its towns; town exceptions are on each card.
aging.description: Connecticut’s five Area Agencies on Aging serve lists of towns. They help older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers with information, benefits counseling, caregiver support and in-home services.
aging.next_step_extra: The statewide CHOICES line, 1-800-994-9422, also reaches the agency serving your town.

programs.name: Connecticut veterans: Office of Advocacy and Assistance for claims help
programs.organization: Connecticut Department of Veterans Affairs, Office of Advocacy and Assistance
programs.description: Accredited Veteran Service Officers in five district offices (Rocky Hill, Norwich, Milford, Fairfield and Waterbury) help veterans and families with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and state benefits at no charge. Each town also names a Municipal Veterans Representative who can point you to help.
programs.next_step: Choose a county above for its district office, or call the Office of Advocacy and Assistance at 860-616-3685.
constraints: Districts follow congressional district lines, so a few towns in a county use a different office; the county card names them.

programs.name: CHOICES and Connecticut’s Area Agencies on Aging
programs.organization: Connecticut Department of Aging and Disability Services and the five Area Agencies on Aging
programs.description: CHOICES is Connecticut’s statewide line for aging and long-term care questions. It is a partnership of the Department of Aging and Disability Services, the Center for Medicare Advocacy and the Area Agencies on Aging. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call CHOICES at 1-800-994-9422, or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (CHOICES, Connecticut’s SHIP)
programs.organization: Connecticut Department of Aging and Disability Services, CHOICES
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from CHOICES, Connecticut’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, through the Area Agencies on Aging.
programs.next_step: Call CHOICES at 1-800-994-9422, or the Area Agency on Aging that serves your town. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

sources.title: Connecticut ADS: CHOICES brochure (2022)
sources.scope: Questions about Medicare? Call CHOICES at 1-800-994-9422 or your Area Agency on Aging; search excerpt.

programs.name: Connecticut Long Term Care Ombudsman and elder abuse reporting
programs.organization: Connecticut Long Term Care Ombudsman Program; Department of Social Services, Protective Services for the Elderly
programs.description: Free, confidential advocacy for residents of nursing homes, residential care homes and assisted living. Protective Services for the Elderly takes reports of abuse, neglect, exploitation or abandonment of people 60 and older living in the community.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman at 1-866-388-1888. To report elder abuse, call Protective Services for the Elderly at 1-888-385-4225 (weekdays 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.); after hours, call 2-1-1. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for Connecticut veterans and older adults
programs.description: Statewide Legal Services is the usual entry point for free civil legal aid in Connecticut. It gives advice by phone or refers callers to a local legal services office or private attorney at no cost.
programs.next_step: Call Statewide Legal Services at 1-800-453-3320 (860-344-0380 from Middletown and Hartford). People 60 and older can also call 2-1-1 for the nearest elder law office.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type.

sources.title: CTLawHelp: About Legal Aid in Connecticut
sources.scope: Statewide Legal Services, 1-800-453-3320 or 860-344-0380, the entry point for legal assistance; search excerpt.

sources.title: Connecticut ADS: Affordable legal help
sources.scope: Statewide Legal Services 800-453-3320; over 60, visit CTLawHelp or call 2-1-1; search excerpt.

programs.name: VA health care in Connecticut
programs.organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Connecticut Healthcare System
programs.description: Connecticut veterans are served by the VA Connecticut Healthcare System: the West Haven VA Medical Center (950 Campbell Avenue; 203-932-5711) and the Newington campus (555 Willard Avenue; 860-666-6951), with community clinics.
programs.next_step: For appointments, call 866-808-7921. Not enrolled yet? Ask a Veteran Service Officer for help applying.
constraints: If a service you need is not offered near you, ask about travel benefits and community care.
